The Radial Breathing Mode (RBM) in carbon nanotubes refers to a specific vibrational mode where the carbon atoms oscillate radially, akin to the tube "breathing." This mode is particularly significant in Raman spectroscopy for identifying single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWNTs) and characterizing their diameter. The RBM frequencies typically range from 120 to 350 cm⁻¹ for SWNTs with diameters between 0.7 nm and 2 nm. The relationship between RBM frequency and nanotube diameter can be expressed as RBM = A/dt + B, where A and B are experimentally determined parameters (R12.pdf).
